Thank you, Madam Chair. Good morning, everyone. My name is Angela Gardner. General Manager of Utilities Environment Division.
For your consideration this morning is a report on an information report that provides an update on the preparations for the launch of the Curbside Organics Program set for May 2023.

This report provides an overview of the multi-phase communications and education strategy to support the role of the new Curbside Organics Program, the Organics Utility and Associated Curbside Waste Collection Service level changes.
The strategy builds upon the successes of the city's existing waste communications and education plans, as well as the recycling communications program and lessons learned from other jurisdictions.
There are four phases of the strategy that will be used to support the implementation and ensure the long-term success of the program.

Phase one of the strategy is underway and focuses on creating awareness of the upcoming changes to Curbside Waste Services, including year-round by weekly garbage collections and the end of the subscription green card program.
Phase two through four will build upon the first phase to ensure that residents are prepared for and supportive through the changes over the next few years.
The multi-phase approach is intended to provide timely information at the right level of detail so that our residents can take appropriate action at the appropriate time.
For the initial launch and the first year of the program, these activities are funded through the Curbside Organics Capital Project.
Going forward on going operating costs for education and communication will be built into the organics utility rate.
Work is also progressing on finalizing logistics details for the role of the organics program, including plans for delivering smaller cards to eligible townhouse complexes.
A further report on those logistics will be brought to this committee in early 2023.
As part of that work, the administration will be engaging individual counselors to provide insight on any ward specific considerations.
Specific communication and education materials will be developed as we progress through the strategy.

In addition to the city's traditional communications channels, these materials will also be shared in advance with the mayor and counselor so they can also eat a lot of their social media networks to enhance the reach of the program.

This next information report is in response to an inquiry made by Councillor Donnar at City Council on April 26, 2021 to review the current process for issuing drinking water advisories and identify opportunities to further improve the processes to ensure the safety of residents during water disruption events.

The water outage notification system is a framework that was developed in conjunction with the water security agency and public health to notify impacted property owners of water service outages and the associated risks of potential water quality and safety for customers connected to the city's water distribution network.
The process includes issuing yellow notices to indicate the location dates and time the drinking water advisory was issued.
Information on what to do when the service when the water service returns and instructions on how to safely use the water until the water quality tests have passed and service returns to normal.

Once all water quality tests have passed, all customers who received the yellow drinking water advisory notice are notified via a hand delivered green drinking water advisory lifted notice that they can resume water normal water usage.
The specific steps of the process are outlined in appendix three of the report.
Earlier this year, an audit of the city's management of drinking water advisories was completed by water security agency.
Two findings related to calibration of field test equipment and water security agency sign-off of the established standard operating procedures were identified and are being addressed.

In March 2021, City Council approved, in principle, the urban forest management plan that examined the state of the city's urban forest and outlined the strategies to plan, grow, manage and protect the city's trees and canopy.
The implementation plan presents a pathway to address the goals of the urban forest management plan by identifying specific initiatives and timelines over the next 10 years.
Next slide please. The plan identifies 18 actions that the city and community can take to create a sustainable urban forest.
These actions and 131 associated initiatives have been organized into five key areas that include planning, growing, managing, protecting and reimagining the urban forest.
Initiatives within the planning area will improve the planning for future of the urban forest through process improvements that increase and improve space for trees.
Initiatives within the growing area will support an increased amount of tree planting and tree species diversity.
Initiatives within the managing area will improve maintenance, pruning, watering, enhanced service levels and improve the tree inventory.
Initiatives within the protecting area will formalize tree protection through a bylaw providing improved tree protection processes, education and asset preservation.
Initiatives within the reimagining area will enhance the social and cultural connections between the urban forest and the community. Next slide please.
